issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares the Pneumatic interface method as releasePressure(): void (problem_statement.md lines 16-19), but elsewhere in the same problem statement (remarks) the method name openValve() is used (problem_statement.md lines 70-71). The reference solution implements Pneumatic with openValve() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java) and the launched ride classes implement openValve() as well. This name mismatch (releasePressure vs openValve) is an internal contradiction in the specification and a cross-artifact inconsistency: students reading the UML may declare releasePressure(), while the solution and remarks expect openValve(). That will confuse students and can make automated tests fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Pneumatic interface method name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (a) update the UML and problem text to use openValve() instead of releasePressure(), or (b) change the solution and remarks to implement releasePressure() instead of openValve(). Preferably align the UML to openValve() (as used in the solution and remarks) so students and tests are consistent.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares the Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and releasePressure(), but the solution implements Pneumatic with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(). The method name openValve() in the solution (and its overrides in LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) refers to the same conceptual operation as releasePressure() in the problem/UML, yet uses a different identifier. This naming divergence prevents a straightforward mapping from the UML/problem requirements to the provided solution code and would confuse students implementing the exercise according to the UML.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the identifier names so the interface and implementations match the UML/problem statement. Rename openValve() in the solution to releasePressure(), and update the Pneumatic interface and all implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) accordingly. Alternatively, if openValve() is the intended name, update the problem statement/UML to use openValve() instead of releasePressure().
